main.claim: Fill in your name, title, company, phone, email, website and links, pick one of four templates, and check the live preview. Copy the signature as rich text and paste it into Gmail, Outlook or Apple Mail, or copy the HTML.

sections.heading: How to make an email signature
sections.body:
Open the [email signature generator](https://email-signature.lazur.app/) in your browser. The form on the left holds your details. Fill in the fields you want to show, and leave the rest blank.

1. Enter your name, job title, company, phone number and email address.
2. Add your website, and your LinkedIn and X links if you use them.
3. Paste a photo URL if you want a picture in the signature.
4. Pick an accent colour for the lines and links.
5. Choose one of the four templates: Classic, Modern, Minimal or Bold.
6. Look at the live preview on the right. It updates as you type.
7. Copy the signature when it looks right.

You only need a few lines. Most people use name, title, company, one phone number and one email. Extra links make the signature longer, and a long signature can push your message down on a phone.

sections.heading: Pick a template with your real details
sections.body:
The four templates use the same fields, so the choice comes down to how the signature looks with your text. Try each one with your real name and company. A long job title or a long company name can look very different from one template to the next.

Check the preview at the size you will read it. Then look again after you add a photo. A photo takes up more room than text, so the template that looks best with text alone may not look best with a picture.

sections.heading: Copy it into your email app
sections.body:
Use **Copy as rich text** when you want the layout, colours and links to carry over. Paste it into the signature settings of your email app. The steps for the three most common apps are on their own pages:

- [Gmail signature](https://email-signature.lazur.app/gmail)
- [Outlook signature](https://email-signature.lazur.app/outlook)
- [Apple Mail signature](https://email-signature.lazur.app/mac-mail)

If the rich text paste loses the layout, copy the HTML instead and check the result again in a test email.

sections.heading: Test it before you rely on it
sections.body:
Send yourself one email from the account that will use the signature. Open it on your computer and on your phone. Check that the name, phone number and links are correct, that the photo shows, and that the links open. Then reply to that email to check how the signature looks under a quoted message.

If you use more than one address, set up the signature for each account, because each email app stores signatures on its own.

pages.title: Email Signature Generator with Logo | Lazur
pages.description: Add a logo to your email signature with a picture link. Pick a template, check the live preview, then copy the signature into Gmail, Outlook or Apple Mail.
pages.claim: Paste a link to your logo image into the photo URL field, pick a template, and check the live preview. The tool does not upload a file from your computer, so the logo needs to be online first.

sections.heading: Add a logo with an image link
sections.body:
The generator has a photo URL field. Use it for your logo. The field needs a link to an image that is already on the web, not a file on your computer.

1. Find your logo on your company website or another public page that shows it.
2. Copy the link to the image file itself. It usually ends in .png, .jpg or .webp, but some links do not show an extension.
3. Open the [email signature generator](https://email-signature.lazur.app/) and paste the link into the photo URL field.
4. Check the live preview. If the logo shows there, it will load in your signature.

**If the preview is empty,** the link probably points to a web page that holds the image, not to the image file. Go back to the image and copy its own address.

sections.heading: Choose a size that fits the text
sections.body:
A logo can take over a signature. Look at the preview with your name and phone number beside it. If the logo is wide and the text looks small, the logo is too big for the template.

You can pick a different template and compare. Minimal has less going on around the logo than Bold, so try both and keep the one that reads most easily at a glance.

The logo also needs to work at phone width. Many people read email on a phone, and a logo that fills the top of the screen pushes your text far down. Check the preview at a narrow width if you can, or send yourself a test and open it on your phone. If your name is hard to read at that size, use a smaller logo or a template with less space around the photo.

sections.heading: Paste the logo signature into your email app
sections.body:
Copy the signature with **Copy as rich text**, then paste it into the signature settings of your email app. The logo comes with it when the paste keeps the image link.

After you paste, send a test email to yourself. Some email apps block images until the reader chooses to show them, so the logo may not appear on the first view. That is normal for images in email. Your text and links should still show.

sections.heading: When the logo does not paste
sections.body:
If the logo is missing after you paste, copy the HTML instead and paste it in the signature box. Some apps accept HTML code only in certain places, so check the result in a test email.

If the logo still does not show, put the logo on a page you control, copy its image link again, and paste the new link into the generator. Then copy the signature again and replace the old one.

faq.q: Can I upload a logo file to the generator?
faq.a: No. The photo URL field takes a link to an image that is already online. Put your logo on your website or another public page, copy the link to the image file, and paste that link into the field.

faq.q: Will my logo show in Gmail and Outlook?
faq.a: It can. Both apps load images from a link, but some apps hold back images until the reader allows them. Send a test email to yourself in each app you use and check that the logo appears.

faq.q: Do I need a logo to have a good signature?
faq.a: No. A name, title, company, phone number and email address make a clear signature by themselves. Add a logo only if your company uses one in its other materials, and keep it small.

pages.title: Email Signature Generator for Outlook | Lazur
pages.description: Make an email signature for Outlook, then paste it into the Outlook signature settings and set it as the default for new messages and replies.
pages.claim: Build your signature in the generator, click Copy as rich text, then paste it under Signatures in Outlook. In Outlook for Windows, you can set it as the default for new messages and replies in the same settings.

sections.heading: Paste the signature into Outlook for Windows
sections.body:
Build the signature in the [generator](https://email-signature.lazur.app/outlook) first, then copy it. Open Outlook and follow these steps:

1. Open a new message.
2. Select the **Message** tab.
3. In the **Include** group, select **Signature**, then select **Signatures**.
4. Select **New**, type a name for the signature, and press OK.
5. Click in the **Edit signature** box and paste your signature.
6. Select **OK** to save it.

The name you type is what you will see in the signature list, so pick one that helps you tell your signatures apart, such as Work or Short.

sections.heading: Set the default for new messages and replies
sections.body:
A default signature is added to every new message without you choosing it. In the same **Signatures** window, find the **Choose default signature** section.

Choose the signature for **New messages** and the one for **Replies/forwards**. You can use the same signature for both, or pick a shorter one for replies. Select **Save**, then select **OK**.

When you reopen a message, check the signature at the bottom before you send. If it is not there, the default was not saved for that account.

sections.heading: Outlook on the web and the new Outlook
sections.body:
Outlook on the web and the newer Outlook app keep signatures in the settings menu, not the Message tab. The steps can change between versions, so look for the Signature option in your settings. In one common path, you open Settings, choose Email or Mail, then Compose and reply, and paste the signature there.

If you cannot find the option, search Settings for the word signature. Then paste the signature and send a test message to yourself.

sections.heading: If the layout breaks in Outlook
sections.body:
Sometimes a signature looks right in the preview and wrong in Outlook. Spacing, fonts or the photo can shift when the signature is pasted. Send a test message to yourself and open it in Outlook to check.

If the layout is off, copy the HTML from the generator and paste that instead, or switch to a simpler template with less spacing. Keep the photo small, because large images are the most common reason a layout breaks. A plain signature with four or five lines is the safest choice for Outlook, because it has fewer parts that can shift when Outlook reads the paste. Keep a copy of the signature text in a note as well, so you can paste it again if you ever need to rebuild it. Your signature stays in Outlook on that computer, so change it there too when you update your title or phone number. Keep the title and company lines current, because an old job title is one of the most common signature mistakes after a move.

faq.q: How do I add a signature in Outlook?
faq.a: In Outlook for Windows, open a new message, select the Message tab, choose Include, then Signature, then Signatures. Select New, give it a name, paste your signature into the box, and select OK. Then choose it as your default.

faq.q: Can I set one signature for new emails and another for replies?
faq.a: Yes, in Outlook for Windows. In the Signatures window, the Choose default signature section lets you pick one signature for new messages and another for replies and forwards.

faq.q: Why does my signature look different in Outlook?
faq.a: Outlook has its own rules for fonts, spacing and images. Send a test message to yourself and check it in Outlook. A simpler template with a smaller photo usually fixes most layout problems.

pages.title: Email Signature Generator for College Students | Lazur
pages.description: Make a simple email signature for college with your name, school, major and email. Pick a template, check the preview, then copy it into your email app.
pages.h1: Email signature generator for college students
pages.claim: Enter your name, your school in the company field, your major or year in the title field, and your email. Pick a template and copy the signature into Gmail, Outlook or Apple Mail. Keep it to four or five lines.

sections.heading: What a student signature should include
sections.body:
A student signature has a simple job. It tells the reader who you are and how to reach you. Here is a layout that works for most students:

- Your full name on the first line.
- Your major and year, or your role, such as Research Assistant.
- Your school name.
- Your school email and one phone number, if you want calls.
- Your LinkedIn link, if you use it for jobs or internships.

Skip the quote, the photo and the long list of social icons. Recruiters and professors read the top few lines first, so put your name and school there. Anything below the fourth line is easy to miss, so save extra links for your resume.

sections.heading: Fill in the generator
sections.body:
Open the [email signature generator](https://email-signature.lazur.app/college-students) and enter your details:

1. Name in the name field.
2. Your major and year, or role, in the title field.
3. Your school in the company field.
4. Your email and phone number.
5. LinkedIn link, if you have one.
6. Pick a template and check the live preview.

Try the Minimal template first. It keeps the text easy to scan, which suits a signature you will use for applications and class emails.

sections.heading: Check your school's rules
sections.body:
Some schools publish their own email signature rules, with a required logo, fonts or wording. Several universities offer their own signature forms for students and staff. Before you add a school logo or a seal, check your school's IT or brand page. If your school has a form, use its layout and the generator for the rest.

If your school has no rules, a plain text signature with your name, major, school and email is enough. Update the signature each year when your year changes, so the details stay accurate for your next internship or job.

sections.heading: Add it to your email app
sections.body:
Click **Copy as rich text** in the generator, then paste the signature in your email app's settings. Each app stores it in a different place:

- [Gmail](https://email-signature.lazur.app/gmail)
- [Outlook](https://email-signature.lazur.app/outlook)
- [Apple Mail on Mac](https://email-signature.lazur.app/mac-mail)

When you are done, send a test email to your school address and to a personal address. Some school email systems add their own footer under your signature, so look at the whole message, not only the signature. Check how it looks on your phone too, since many students read email there first. If the signature runs past four or five lines on the phone, remove the least important line first. That is usually the phone number, because the email address already gives the reader a way to reply.

faq.q: What should a college student put in an email signature?
faq.a: Put your name, major and year or role, school name, school email and one phone number. Add a LinkedIn link if you use it for jobs. Keep it to four or five lines so it is easy to read on a phone.

faq.q: Should I add my school logo?
faq.a: Only if your school allows it. Some schools have their own rules for logos and seals. Check your school's brand or IT page first. The logo page on this site explains how to add an image link.

faq.q: Is a signature useful for internships and job emails?
faq.a: Yes. A signature with your name, school, major and LinkedIn link gives the reader what they need without an extra message. Keep it plain, so it looks professional in every app you use.

pages.title: Email Signature Generator for Gmail | Lazur
pages.description: Make a Gmail signature in the browser, copy it as rich text, and paste it into Gmail Settings. Step by step, with the Save Changes button you need.
pages.claim: Build your signature in the generator, click Copy as rich text, then go to Gmail Settings, See all settings, General, and paste it in the Signature box. Click Save Changes at the bottom of the page.

sections.heading: Paste the signature into Gmail
sections.body:
Build your signature in the [generator](https://email-signature.lazur.app/gmail) and copy it. Then open Gmail on your computer and follow these steps. Google's own help page uses the same path.

1. Click **Settings** at the top right of Gmail.
2. Click **See all settings**.
3. Stay on the **General** tab and scroll to the **Signature** section.
4. Click in the signature box and paste your signature.
5. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click **Save Changes**.

If you already have a signature, it is replaced by the one in the box. Copy your old signature first if you want to keep it. Paste the new one over it, then click Save Changes. If the signature looks different in Gmail than in the generator, reopen the Settings page and check that the paste did not add extra blank lines.

sections.heading: Choose the signature for each account
sections.body:
Gmail lets you send from more than one address. If you use Send mail as, choose the address from the drop-down menu above the signature box on the Settings page. Each address can have its own signature.

If you do not see the drop-down, check the Send mail as section on the Accounts and Import settings page, then return to the Signature section.

sections.heading: Switch signatures while you write
sections.body:
When you write a message, look for the pen icon, labelled Insert signature, at the bottom of the compose window. Click it to pick a different signature for that message. This is useful if you keep a short signature for replies and a full one for new emails.

Gmail help says you can set a default for new emails and another for replies. The steps are in the signature settings on the same Settings page, so look there if your default is not what you expect. Gmail's Settings page is also where you change or delete a signature later. Under General, select the signature to edit it, then click Save Changes.

sections.heading: Fix images and length
sections.body:
Images count toward Gmail's limit of 10,000 characters for a signature. If you paste a signature with a large photo and Gmail shows an error, resize the photo or remove it. Then try again.

After you save, send a test email to yourself and open it in Gmail on your phone. A short signature with a small photo usually shows the best result on every screen. Gmail settings are saved to your account, so the same signature should appear on other computers signed in to that account. Check once on each computer you use, because a browser extension or an older tab can show a stale copy until you reload.

faq.q: Where do I add a signature in Gmail?
faq.a: Click Settings at the top right, then See all settings. On the General tab, scroll to Signature, paste your signature into the box, and click Save Changes at the bottom of the page.

faq.q: Why won't my Gmail signature save?
faq.a: The most common cause is size. Gmail limits a signature to 10,000 characters, and images count toward that limit. Resize or remove a large image, then try again and click Save Changes.

faq.q: Can I use different signatures in Gmail?
faq.a: Yes. You can change the signature for each send-as address in Settings, and you can use the Insert signature pen icon in the compose window to pick a different one for a single message.

pages.title: Email Signature Generator for iPhone | Lazur
pages.description: Make a signature for the iPhone Mail app. Learn where the Signature setting is, what formatting carries over, and how to remove Sent from my iPhone.
pages.claim: Build your signature in the generator, then copy it into Settings, Mail, Signature on your iPhone. The iPhone signature box holds little formatting, so keep the signature short and check it in a test email.

sections.heading: Where the signature goes on iPhone
sections.body:
Build the signature in the [generator](https://email-signature.lazur.app/iphone) first. Then open the iPhone's Settings app and follow these steps:

1. Tap **Settings**.
2. Scroll down and tap **Mail**.
3. Tap **Signature**.
4. Delete the text in the box, then paste your signature.

On some iOS versions the path shows the Mail app under Apps. Look for Mail and then Signature if the menu looks different. If you cannot find the Mail setting, use the search bar at the top of Settings and type Signature. Set the signature on each iPhone and iPad you use, because the setting is saved on each device.

sections.heading: Keep the formatting simple
sections.body:
The signature box in iPhone Settings has very little formatting. You can not change colours or fonts there, and images usually do not carry over from a pasted design. A template with bold colours and a photo may look different on the phone than in the preview.

For the iPhone, keep the signature to plain text: your name, title, company, phone number and email. Paste the rich text version first. If the layout breaks, delete it and type the plain version by hand. A clean line of text is easier to read on a small screen. Short lines wrap less, so put each detail on its own line and avoid long links that run off the edge.

sections.heading: Remove Sent from my iPhone
sections.body:
Apple adds the words Sent from my iPhone to messages you send from Mail by default. You can change that text in the same Signature box. Replace it with your own signature, or delete it and leave the box blank if you do not want any sign-off.

A signature that you write yourself is often a better fit for work email, because it gives the reader your name and title rather than only the device.

sections.heading: Check it on your phone
sections.body: Send yourself an email from the Mail app on your iPhone after you save the signature. Open it on the phone, then open it again on your computer to compare. Check the name, the phone number, the links and the line breaks. Tap each link to make sure it opens the right page. If the signature looks wrong, delete it in Settings, paste the plain version again, and send another test. Going back and forth between the phone and the generator is normal, because each test shows one more thing to adjust. Keep the final version in a note on your phone, so you can paste it again quickly after an iOS update or when you set up a new phone.

faq.q: How do I create an email signature on my iPhone?
faq.a: Open Settings, tap Mail, then tap Signature. Delete the text in the box and paste or type your signature. Then send a test email from the Mail app to check how it looks.

faq.q: Can I add a photo or logo to an iPhone Mail signature?
faq.a: The signature box in iPhone Settings has little formatting. Photos and custom fonts usually do not carry over from a designed signature, so use plain text on the phone and keep your designed signature for the computer.

faq.q: How do I remove Sent from my iPhone?
faq.a: Open Settings, tap Mail, then tap Signature. Delete the Sent from my iPhone text, and leave the box blank or type your own signature. The change applies to messages you send from the Mail app on that device.

pages.title: Email Signature Generator for Mac Mail | Lazur
pages.description: Make a signature for Apple Mail on Mac. Copy it from the generator, paste it under Mail Settings, Signatures, and choose it for each new message.
pages.h1: Email signature generator for Mac Mail
pages.claim: Build your signature in the generator, click Copy as rich text, then paste it in Mail, Settings, Signatures. Select the account, click the plus button, and paste the signature into the right-hand box.

sections.heading: Add the signature in Mail on Mac
sections.body:
Build the signature in the [generator](https://email-signature.lazur.app/mac-mail) and copy it. Then open the Mail app on your Mac and follow these steps. Apple's Mail help uses the same menu names.

1. Choose **Mail**, then **Settings**.
2. Click **Signatures**.
3. In the left column, select the email account you want to use the signature with.
4. Click the **Add** button (the plus sign) below the middle column, and type a name for the signature. The name shows in the Signature pop-up menu when you write a message.
5. In the right column, click **Edit** in the menu bar, choose **Paste**, and check the result.

If **All Signatures** is selected in the left column, drag the new signature onto the account before you use it.

sections.heading: Choose the signature when you write
sections.body:
When you start a new message, open the Signature pop-up menu in the message window and pick the signature you want. Each message can use a different one. Use the short version for replies and the full one for new messages. If you send from a work account and a personal one, give the signatures names that show which is which, such as Work and Personal. The name is what you see in the menu, so a clear name stops a work signature from going out on a personal account.

To keep your signature below the text you are replying to, turn off the option named Place signature above quoted text in the Signatures settings. Leave it on if you want the signature above the quoted message.

sections.heading: Format the signature in the Mail app
sections.body:
You can change the font, colour, alignment and lists in the right-hand box with the Format menu. Use this to fix small problems, such as a line that is too large or spacing that looks off. Keep the changes modest so the signature still reads well on a phone. Test the final version by sending it to a second email account. How a signature looks in Mail can differ from how it looks in Gmail or on an iPhone, so one check in each place saves you from a message that looks wrong. Keep a plain text copy in a note, so you can paste it again quickly if you need to rebuild it.

If the paste changes the layout, use the Format menu to correct it, then send a test message to yourself and open it in Mail.

sections.heading: Turn your voice into text on Mac
sections.body: If you write many emails by speaking, Lazur is a Mac app that does this in any app on your Mac. Hold two keys and talk, and it types what you said where your cursor is, including in Mail.

faq.q: How do I create an email signature in Mail on Mac?
faq.a: Choose Mail, then Settings, then Signatures. Select your account, click the plus button, name the signature, then choose Edit and Paste in the right-hand box. Your signature is ready to pick when you write a message.

faq.q: Why can't I choose a signature in Mail on my Mac?
faq.a: The signature must belong to the account you are sending from. Open Mail, Settings, Signatures, select that account in the left column, and check that the signature is listed under it. If All Signatures is selected, drag the signature onto the account.

faq.q: Can I use a different signature for each Mail account?
faq.a: Yes. Create a signature under each account in the Signatures settings. When you write a message, open the Signature pop-up menu and choose the one for the account you are sending from.
